title: Registry index meta — /registry/index/meta.json
description: The registry index's table of contents: the shard list, registry-wide counts, and the delist set the badge route uses as a belt-and-braces guard against a stale cached badge (FS10-032 — the edge keeps this document hot in KV as `registry-index-meta`). Counts include `detected` repositories in `totals.detected` only; they are never listed (GH-014).

source.description: Which plane produced this artifact. `sample` and `fixture` declare a NON-PRODUCTION plane: every page that renders such an artifact is labelled sample, and a production deployment refuses to serve it (FS-10 §2 v0 note; the edge route answers `sandbox_artifact_on_prod`). `registry-v0` is the P-M2 production source of record — the curated registry repository the index is built from. Optional, and its absence asserts nothing: an artifact whose body cannot carry the label borrows the plane's declaration from `/registry/index/meta.json`. The enum widens additively when the P-M3 producer takes a value of its own.

shards.description: Every shard document that exists, with its entry count. A browse client fetches only the shards it needs.

exportUrl.description: The bulk export document (same shape as a shard, `shard: "export"`).

listed.description: Repositories that appear in a shard: verified + suspended + quit + delisted.

detected.description: Detected-but-unclaimed repositories. Counted here and nowhere else (GH-014; URS §21 OPEN-33 governs whether they ever enter exports).

delisted.description: Node ids of every listed repository whose state is `suspended`, `quit` or `delisted`. The badge route serves the neutral form for any id in this set even if a cached badge artifact still says otherwise (FS10-032). All three states render neutral — a stale badge never keeps asserting registration (WEB-085) — so the guard has to cover all three; the member keeps its name, which is the state a reader recognises. *(Wording corrected 2026-09-08: it said `delisted` or `quit`, and a suspended repository would have kept a registered badge alive on a cache.)*

githubNodeId.description: A GitHub GraphQL node_id, in either of the two forms GitHub has issued: the opaque current form (a repository's is `R_`-prefixed) and the legacy base64 form, whose decoded value begins `010:Repository` and whose `=` padding the first alternative cannot express. Widened 2026-09-08 to admit the second: `registry-v0-record.v1` accepts both, so a record the curated registry accepts is publishable in this artifact. The primary key for repositories and people throughout this contract set (FS-00 §6.1).
